correctness.rationale: Normalized Bloch and rotation axes have dot product zero and cross n × r=(-3,2,-1)/sqrt(14). Consequently J=(2,-1)^T/sqrt(14), v=(0,-1)^T, J^T J=5/14, J^T v=1/sqrt(14), c^T J=1/sqrt(14), and s_E=1/(5+14 lambda)>0. Independently reconstructed these exact identities symbolically; H^2=2I, E^2=3/2 gives -2 Var(H)=-1. For any one-term H=cO, s_E=||j||^2/(||j||^2+lambda)*v_H<=0 for lambda>0; zero-row and lambda=0 least-squares degeneracies also cannot ascend. The source checker was inspected and is ancillary. Claim is a local directional, not an accepted step, result.

value.rationale: The exact obstruction isolates projected-vector geometry from sampling, truncation and solver error, and proves that two nonconstant Hamiltonian terms are the smallest possible setting. This mathematically explains why a descent safeguard can be necessary even with exact observables; no typicality or source algorithm failure is inferred.

final_claim: For exact termwise Hamiltonian-pool OVQITE on a one-qubit pure state, the explicit two-term H=Y+Z, Bloch r=(-1,-2,-1)/sqrt(6), ansatz axis n=(2,1,-4)/sqrt(21) yields strictly uphill exact energy derivative s_E=1/(5+14 lambda) at every regularization lambda>=0 although imaginary-time energy derivative is -1; no one-term Hamiltonian pool can point strictly uphill.
limitations: Local derivative only; Armijo-accepted steps and statistical performance are not refuted.
No universal rate/frequency result for multi-term Hamiltonian pools.
